## On Hilbert's 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 75 results has its exact statement, its status (proved, conditional, open or counterexample), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the LaTeX file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.0.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [On Hilbert's 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/index.html.md): by Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov (2026). Hilbert's sixth problem from Kolmogorov's axioms and the Boltzmann equation to the Navier Stokes equations, and the inverse passage: Bayesian estimation on the solution manifold of a differential equation, where the adjoint evolution of the data is a sufficient statistic for linear equations. Keywords: Hilbert's sixth problem, foundations of probability, kinetic theory, Boltzmann equation, Navier Stokes equations, hydrodynamic limits, Bayesian inverse problems, sufficient statistics, generative Bayesian computation, large deviations, stochastic mechanics, statistical mechanics.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23327515): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23327515 for version 1.0.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23327514 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page

- [Main result: Adjoint representation of the sufficient statistic](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#adjoint_representation_of_the_sufficient_statistic): Lemma 15.1, page 206, proved. For a linear evolution equation that is diagonal in a fixed basis, the data statistic that is sufficient for the initial state is the coefficient vector of the time zero value of the solution of the backward adjoint equation driven by the data as point sources.
- [Main result: Exact sufficiency, linear case](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#exact_sufficiency_linear_case): Proposition 15.2, page 207, proved. In the linear model with a Gaussian prior the adjoint statistic is sufficient, the posterior given it is the full data posterior, and the conditional quantile map is exactly affine with slope equal to the posterior covariance.
- [Main result: Equivalence of the one step efficient score summary with the efficient centering](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#equivalence_with_the_efficient_centering): Proposition 15.5, page 210, proved. Under explicit regularity, rate and Lipschitz conditions, the cross fitted one step efficient score summary agrees with the efficient centering of Nickl's Bernstein von Mises theorem to order smaller than the root N scale in a negative Sobolev norm, so it is a computable center of the Gaussian limit of the posterior.
- [Main result: Jiang Wong under a uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption: the posterior mean summary is asymptotically sufficient](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#jiang_wong_under_bernstein_von_mises): Theorem 15.38, page 256, conditional. If a Bernstein von Mises theorem holds uniformly over prior typical truths, then conditioning on the posterior mean alone, or on any summary root N equivalent to it, loses nothing at the root N scale: the recentered posterior given the summary and the recentered posterior given all of the data have the same Gaussian limit in Wasserstein distance.
- [Main result: Effective dimension under dissipation](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#effective_dimension_under_dissipation): Theorem 15.46, page 267, conditional. For the heat and Stokes equations on the torus with a power law prior, the number of modes in which the data at least halve the prior variance grows like a power of the sample size divided by viscosity times observation time, so dissipation lowers the effective dimension; for a nonlinear forward map, under a uniform Bernstein von Mises hypothesis and assumptions on the training residuals and the summary, a generator need only learn the posterior scale on those modes (in the linear model it needs no training), and the cost of using the prior spread beyond them is bounded explicitly.
- [Main result: Transfer of Bernstein von Mises guarantees to the GBC posterior (BvM for GBC)](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#bvm_for_gbc): Theorem 16.2, page 275, proved. If the posterior produced by a generative Bayesian computation (GBC) generator is closer to the exact posterior than the root N scale in Wasserstein distance and concentrates on the localization set with bounded moments, then it inherits the Bernstein von Mises limit of the exact posterior for the initial condition and, for the reaction diffusion and two dimensional Navier Stokes equations, for the trajectory, with exact asymptotic coverage of its credible bands and, for Navier Stokes, attainment of the local asymptotic minimax bound for bounded losses; nothing is assumed about how the generator was trained.
- [Main result: No uniform guarantee: minimax lower bound for conditional quantile generators over monotone Hölder classes](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#no_uniform_guarantee_for_quantile_generators): Theorem 16.15, page 290, proved. Any generator, trained on M simulated pairs, that must be accurate at a fixed interior summary value for every conditional law in a monotone Hölder class of conditional quantile maps of smoothness beta on a J dimensional summary has, for some map in the class, Wasserstein error at least a constant free of J times (C M) to the power minus beta over (2 beta plus J) with probability at least 1/8, where C bounds the design density, so root N accuracy uniformly over the class requires at least N to the power 1 plus J over (2 beta) simulations divided by C, more than any polynomial once J grows; reading this as the accuracy condition of the transfer theorem uses the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption.
- [Conditional: The one step summary under four ABC criteria: Bayes risk optimal up to o(1), all four attained in the J mode Gaussian projection](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#one_step_summary_under_four_abc_criteria): Proposition 15.29, page 244
- [Conditional: Deep PLS structure of the GBC summary](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#deep_pls_structure_of_the_gbc_summary): Proposition 15.34, page 253
- [Conditional: Jiang Wong under a uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption: the posterior mean summary is asymptotically sufficient](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#jiang_wong_under_bernstein_von_mises): Theorem 15.38, page 256
- [Conditional: GBC with the posterior mean summary](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#gbc_with_the_posterior_mean_summary): Corollary 15.40, page 258
- [Conditional: The Gaussian comparison models admitted by the first hypothesis of the nonlinear sufficiency gap bounds](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#sufficiency_gap_admissible_gaussian_models): Proposition 15.43, page 261
- [Conditional: A sufficient condition for the nonlinear sufficiency gap hypotheses in terms of the centering](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#sufficiency_gap_hypotheses_from_centering_clt): Lemma 15.44, page 263
- [Counterexample: A two coordinate model in which the sufficiency gap hypotheses depend on the summary](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#two_coordinate_model_sufficiency_gap_depends_on_summary): Proposition 15.45, page 264
- [Conditional: Effective dimension under dissipation](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#effective_dimension_under_dissipation): Theorem 15.46, page 267
- [Conditional: Sufficiency versus the raw data: simulation cost of a generator trained without a summary](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#sufficiency_versus_the_raw_data): Theorem 15.47, page 269
- [Conditional: Solve then simulate equals simulate the limit: tangent linear forward simulation of GBC draws](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#solve_then_simulate_equals_simulate_the_limit): Corollary 16.4, page 280
- [Conditional: Bernstein von Mises for the identity skip Gaussian head quantile generator, conditional on the uniform hypothesis](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#bernstein_von_mises_for_the_identity_skip_quantile_generator): Theorem 16.10, page 285
- [Open: Beyond the plane wave: information operator of cubic NLS about a multimode background](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#beyond_the_plane_wave): Open Question 17.12, page 371
- [Conditional: Two limit convergence of the regression summary (least squares Monte Carlo and GBC)](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#two_limit_convergence_of_the_regression_summary): Theorem 17.14, page 373
- [Open: Uniformity: the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption and related open hypotheses](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#uniformity): Open Question 17.18, page 380

- [Open: Open problem: uniform entropy production bound for the Kac walk on conditioned products of normal scale mixtures](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#open_problem_kac_entropy_production_ggc_mixtures): Open Problem 8, page 446
- [Open: Open problem: posterior contraction and Bernstein von Mises theorems for the initial vorticity of two dimensional Navier Stokes from fixed sensors](https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/results.html#open_problem_ns_posterior_fixed_sensors): Open Problem 10, page 447
